record.question: What can standardized author-purpose questions validate?
record.what_happened: What standardized author-purpose questions can validate: kill. Licensed by G01, A06, H13, P14; the transfer gap is V13 has ground truth for private process by construction; a standardized question has ground truth only for the normative target..
record.what_changed_in_the_project_world: A text-side design is exported with its gap, its records, its baseline and its failure meaning attached; nothing here is human evidence.
record.what_remains_a_rival: if they do not dissociate in construction, the question measures one thing and the distinction is idle

hypothesis: Standardized author-purpose questions are given a corpus blueprint and a ceiling: reader competence, not creator-history truth.

G01.what_happened: With twelve artifacts and their claims' truths, the reader named the maker's stance 85% of the time against 14% chance; a surface classifier on the artifacts named it 16%.

A06.what_happened: The best first cue for novices was random and for experts random; after every cue the posteriors agreed to within 0.00 nats regardless of entry.

H13.what_happened: On artifacts that were literally the same, a classifier named the history 50% of the time against 50% chance, and the artifact-only reader's topology posterior stayed flat.

P14.what_happened: On identical artifacts the reader's top regime mass was 0.50 (abstention); after the separating artifacts it was 0.97 where the alternative method was distinguishable (30720/130560 of pairs), 0.77 in the borderline band, and 0.55 where methods coincide.

deliverable.title: What standardized author-purpose questions can validate

targets.normative_rhetorical_purpose: what a competent reader is expected to say the text is for; validated against reader agreement, not against the author
targets.reader_interpretation: what a given reader took the text to be for; a reading-profile measurement
targets.private_process: what the author actually did and wanted; recoverable only where records exist (L10) and never from a standardized answer

blueprint: a corpus with expert-adjudicated normative purpose labels
reader-model answers scored against those labels
a separate constructed corpus with planted private process to show the two targets come apart
deliverable.claim_ceiling: useful as a measure of reader competence on normative purpose; not creator-history ground truth
deliverable.transfer_gap: V13 has ground truth for private process by construction; a standardized question has ground truth only for the normative target.
deliverable.sounding_line_target: the author-purpose question set and its scoring
deliverable.records_required: adjudicated normative labels; for private process, records, or nothing
deliverable.positive_gate: on the constructed corpus, normative-purpose accuracy and private-process accuracy dissociate
deliverable.failure_meaning: if they do not dissociate in construction, the question measures one thing and the distinction is idle
deliverable.human_evidence_boundary: a standardized question validates reader competence on a normative target; it cannot certify what any author privately intended

gates.name: no_human_claim_in_the_boundary
gates.detail: a task whose answer is known by construction returns that answer

gates_summary.how_to_read: a gate RECORDS here and does not raise, so an exploratory sweep is never killed mid-run. tests/test_gates.py walks every committed verdict and fails the suite on anything in failed_names or unexpected_passes, which puts the hard stop where a result would become public. THREE categories, and they are not the same thing: failed_names is a control that broke; documented_failures is a gate marked expected_to_fail, which records a KNOWN defect so the evidence travels with the result (S-2's dead manipulation, S-3's fitted threshold); unexpected_passes is a documented defect that has started passing, which means somebody fixed it without updating the gate and is the one nobody would otherwise notice. A skipped gate counts as passing but is reported separately: it means an optional dependency was absent, never that a check succeeded.
